lines: なお、図書館の本を汚したり破いたりしてしまった場合は、ご自分で直さず、そのまま貸出カウンターへお持ちください。
52.en: A damaged library book goes straight to the counter, not repaired by yourself
wrong: Patrons should mend a torn library book themselves before returning it
A damaged library book must be left in the return box overnight
A damaged library book is repaired by the patron at the counter

lines: 木曜日の午後か金曜日の午前であれば、こちらはいつでも伺えます。ご都合のよい日時を、今週中にお知らせいただけますと幸いです。
53.en: Murata can come Thursday or Friday; please tell him your time this week
wrong: Yamashita is asked to visit Murata's company on Thursday afternoon
Murata asks Yamashita to reply by next Tuesday with a time
Murata cannot meet before Friday morning, so Yamashita must wait

lines: 大切なのは、なぜうまくいかなかったのかを、自分の言葉で説明してみることだ。
失敗が役に立つのは、その後に考える時間があってこそなのである。
54.en: Failure helps only when you then think about why it went wrong
wrong: Simply repeating failures is enough to build real skill
Failure should be avoided because it teaches nothing at all
Other people should explain to you why your attempt failed

lines: 夜勤などで朝出すのが難しい方には、管理室でふた付きの専用の箱がある場所をご案内しますので、事前にお申し出ください。
55.en: Those who cannot put trash out in the morning should tell the office beforehand
wrong: Those people may put trash out the night before under a net
Those people must apply to the city for a special pickup
Those people may put trash out any time after eight in the morning

lines: 一方、素人がつい忘れがちなのは、撮る前に皿の周りを片付けることだ。
56.en: Amateurs often forget to clear things from around the plate before shooting
wrong: Amateurs often forget to use several lights at once
Amateurs often forget to check which way the light comes from
Amateurs often forget to bring an expensive camera

lines: ところが最近、若手社員から「仕事の進め方が分からないとき、誰に聞けばいいのか迷う」という声が出てきた。
57.en: Young staff say they hesitate over whom to ask when unsure how to proceed
wrong: Young staff say long commutes leave them unable to concentrate
Young staff say seniors' phone calls are too loud to work near
Young staff say they lack the equipment to make documents at home

lines: そうした、わざわざ教えられたわけではない情報から、若手は多くを学んでいたのだ。在宅勤務では、こうした「聞こえてくる学び」がほとんどなくなってしまう。
58.en: Juniors learned much from information nobody deliberately taught them
wrong: Juniors learned mainly from formal lessons given by seniors
Juniors learned by taking recorded training sessions at home
Juniors learned mostly from instructions given in meetings

lines: 大切なのは、在宅か出社かのどちらかを選ぶことではない。それぞれの働き方で何が得られ、何が失われるのかを知ったうえで、うまく組み合わせることだろう。
59.en: Don't pick one; know what each way gains and loses, then combine them
wrong: Everyone should return to the office every day instead of home
Working from home is best, so offices should be dropped entirely
Only the young staff need to come to the office from now on

lines: 写真そのものよりも、写真をきっかけに出てくる話のほうが、町の歴史を知るうえで貴重だったのだ。
60.en: The stories the photos prompted were worth more than the photos
wrong: The photos were worth more than the stories people told
The photos had to be copied because they were fragile
Visitors cared more about the recordings than the photos

lines: そこで今では、展示会の会場に録音機を置き、許可をいただいた方の話を記録している。
61.en: They now record visitors' stories at the exhibition, with their permission
wrong: Visitors now decide where each old photo was taken
They check that each story is true before they record it
They now reenact the festivals that no longer exist

lines: 私たちは、どちらが正しいかをその場で決めず、両方の話をそのまま残すようにしている。
62.en: They don't judge which is right; they keep both accounts as told
wrong: They keep only the version that most people agree on
They check old records and keep only the correct version
They drop conflicting accounts from the record entirely

lines: 読み手が声で場面を決めてしまうと、子どもが自分で想像する余地がなくなるのだという。
63.en: A voice that sets the scene leaves children no room to imagine it themselves
wrong: A dramatic voice startles children and makes them afraid
Reading too well tires the reader before the story ends
Acting out every voice makes the story take far too long

lines: しかし、子どもたちはその方が読み終えると、「あのおばあさん、本当は優しかったんじゃない？」などと、物語について自分から話し始めるのだった。
64.en: After the veteran finished, children began talking about the story on their own
wrong: After the veteran finished, children begged to hear it again
After the veteran finished, children looked bored and unsatisfied
After the veteran finished, children imitated the characters' voices

lines: それ以来、私は声を大げさに変えるのをやめ、ページをめくる前に少し間をとるようにしている。
65.en: The writer stopped exaggerating voices and now pauses before turning each page
wrong: The writer now changes voice for every single character
The writer now asks the children for impressions after reading
The writer now reads with as much emotion as possible

lines: 本が汚れる心配はそれほど大きくない
一冊の本が汚れれば、次に読む人が迷惑する
66.en: A: little worry of dirtying books; B: one dirty book troubles the next reader

lines: ふたのある容器に限るなどのルールを決めておけば
本を守る工夫を先に考えなければならない
67.en: A: allow drinks under rules like lidded cups; B: protect the books first

lines: 毎日使っていたのに、中がどうなっているのか、私はまったく知らなかったのである。
68.en: Though used daily, the writer had no idea how the lamp worked inside
wrong: The writer used it rarely and so knew little about it
The writer knew how it worked but not how to use it
The writer knew its inside well but had never fixed anything

lines: 私は講座に通うようになってから、買い物をするとき、値段や見た目だけでなく、「これは直せるだろうか」と考えるようになった。
69.en: Since the course, the writer also asks whether a thing can be repaired
wrong: Since the course, the writer repairs every broken thing alone
Since the course, the writer chooses only the cheapest things
Since the course, the writer looks only at price and appearance

lines: 直すという経験は、ものを長持ちさせるだけでなく、私たちが何を選んで暮らしているのかを見直すきっかけにもなるのである。
70.en: Repairing makes things last and prompts us to rethink what we choose
wrong: Repairing matters only because it makes things last longer
People should stop buying new things and only repair old ones
Repairing is a pastime that tells us nothing about how we live

lines: 対象：市内に在住・在勤・在学の中学生以上
対象：１８歳以上
71.en: Course 1: city residents/workers/students only; course 3: 18 and over

lines: ①②：１２月１０日（火）９:００から、電話または図書館カウンターで受け付けます。
③：１月１０日（金）必着で、往復はがきでお申し込みください。
72.en: 2: phone or counter from Dec 10; 3: reply postcard arriving by Jan 10
wrong: Both are taken by phone or at the counter from Dec 10
Both need a reply postcard that arrives by Jan 10
2 needs a postcard by Jan 10; 3 is taken by phone or counter

lines: 名簿ですね。じゃあ、それを作ってから和紙を数えます。
73.en: He will make the participant list first, then count the washi paper
wrong: He will count the washi paper first, then make the list
He will order more washi paper from the usual shop
He will rearrange the venue's desks before anything else

lines: じゃあ、明日会社で確認して、また電話します。
74.en: He will check the number at his office tomorrow and call again
wrong: He will book the retest by phone now and check the number later
He will go back to the clinic to pick up his result sheet
He will stop eating from nine tonight and phone tomorrow

lines: まず、もう少し広い言葉で調べ直してみてください。それでも見つからなければ、相談カウンターで司書の方に聞くといいですよ。
75.en: Search again with broader words first; ask a librarian only if that fails
wrong: Ask the librarian first, and search again only if that fails
Search again with narrower words before asking anyone
Skip searching and ask the teacher for more time

lines: それが、イタリアンは一人五千円を超えちゃうので、予約の前に部長に予算を確認しなきゃいけないんです。
76.en: The Italian place is pricey, so she asks the manager about budget before booking
wrong: She books the Italian place provisionally and asks about budget later
She asks the Japanese restaurant about its private room for twenty
She recounts the number of guests before anything else

lines: では、まずこちらの転入届に、新しいご住所とお名前をご記入ください。書き終わりましたら、三番の番号札を取ってお待ちください。
77.en: Write name and new address on the form first, then take a number ticket
wrong: Take number ticket three first, then fill in the form
Go upstairs first to do the child's school procedures
Go to the old city office to get the move-out certificate

lines: 実は、膝を痛めちゃって。医者に、しばらく走るのはやめなさいって言われたの。
78.en: She hurt her knee and the doctor told her to stop running for a while
wrong: Her doctor told her to keep running to strengthen the knee
She hurt her knee but quit on her own, with no advice from a doctor
She hurt her knee at the pool and can no longer swim

lines: 実は、夜九時以降に働けるスタッフが、なかなか見つからないんです。今いる皆さんに無理をしてもらうわけにはいきませんので、思い切って営業時間を短くすることにしました。
79.en: Too few staff can work after nine, so closing time moves earlier
wrong: Evening customers have dropped, so closing time moves earlier
Sales fell from last year, so closing time moves earlier
Closing moves earlier so staff can work longer in the morning

lines: 一番困ったのはインターネット。新しい部屋の接続工事が、三週間先まで予約が取れなくてさ。
80.en: The hardest part was no internet; installation was booked three weeks out
wrong: The hardest part was the city office paperwork, which took weeks
The hardest part was sorting belongings after the movers left
The hardest part was finding a cafe where he could work

lines: それも少しはあると思いますが、一番は、お菓子を小さくしたことですね。
81.en: Online ads helped a little; the main reason was making the sweets smaller
wrong: The main reason was starting to advertise on the internet
The main reason was changing the flavor for young tastes
The main reason was making the sweets twice as large

lines: でも、発表の日が、アルバイトの面接と重なっちゃって。
頼んでみたんだけど、その日しか無理だって。
82.en: The presentation day clashes with a job interview that cannot be moved
wrong: He is not ready for the presentation yet
He thinks next term is a better time to present
He cannot get time off from his part-time job

lines: ほかのお客様のご迷惑になるということもございますが、それ以上に、強い光が繰り返し当たりますと、古い絵の色があせてしまうおそれがあるためです。
83.en: Flash may bother others, but the bigger reason is it may fade old paintings
wrong: Flash is banned mainly because it annoys other visitors
Photography itself has been banned since this month
Flash is dangerous when it is used together with a tripod

lines: 大切なのは、寝る前の一時間をどう過ごすかです。
84.en: What matters is how you spend the hour before bed
wrong: What matters is trying as hard as you can to fall asleep
Counting sheep is the best way to get to sleep
The hour before bed is best spent in a bright room

lines: これまでは、それぞれの店が自分の車で商品を配達していましたが、今後は商店街の組合が一台のトラックで、まとめて配達します。
85.en: Shops used to deliver separately; now the union delivers for all by one truck
wrong: Shops used to share one truck; now each shop delivers alone
The union now sends several trucks, one for each shop
The union has stopped deliveries, so shops use their own cars

lines: そこで来月からは、一つの字を書く回数を減らし、その代わりに、その字を使った短い文を自分で作る宿題に変えます。
86.en: Next month, kanji homework switches to making short sentences with each kanji
wrong: Homework will have more repetitions of each kanji, not fewer
The teacher keeps the homework unchanged, rejecting the complaint
Students will copy short model sentences every night instead

lines: 必要な方には必要な分だけ印刷できるようにしたいと思います。来週から、会議の前日までに申し出ていただければ、紙の資料もご用意します。
87.en: Paper copies will be prepared for those who ask by the day before
wrong: All meeting documents will go back to paper from next week
Paper copies are banned, so attendees must take notes by PC
Paper copies can be requested on the morning of the meeting

lines: 古いものを守るには、ただ大切にしまっておくのではなく、生活の中で使っていくことが必要なのです。
88.en: To protect old things, use them in daily life rather than just storing them
wrong: Old buildings cost too much, so they should be demolished
Old buildings are best kept untouched and stored away
Young people do not want to live in an old town

lines: じゃあ、お先に失礼します。
89.en: The speaker is leaving work before the others
wrong: The speaker is asking the other person to go first
The speaker is heading out on an errand and will return
The speaker is arriving and greeting the others

lines: この資料、明日までに目を通しておいてもらえる？
90.en: She asks him to read through the document by tomorrow
wrong: She asks him to send the document tomorrow
She offers to read the document for him by tomorrow
She asks whether he has already looked at the document

lines: 課長、今ちょっとよろしいでしょうか。
91.en: He asks the section chief whether he has a moment to talk now
wrong: He asks the section chief to look after him from now on
He asks whether the section chief agrees with the plan so far
He thanks the section chief for the time just spent

lines: せっかく来てくれたのに、何のおかまいもできなくて。
92.en: She apologizes for not being able to host the visitor properly
wrong: She complains that the guest came without being invited
She thanks the guest for bringing a gift
She says it was a pity the guest could not come

lines: 駅に着いたら、いったん電話くれる？
93.en: He asks her to phone him once she reaches the station
wrong: He says he will call her once he reaches the station
He asks her to give him the station's phone number
He asks whether she already called him from the station

lines: 雨、降りそうで降らないね。
94.en: It looks like rain but it has not started raining
wrong: It is pouring rain right now
The sky was clear but suddenly it began to rain
It rained heavily even though it did not look like it

lines: このパソコン、使わせていただいてもよろしいですか。
95.en: He asks for permission to use this computer
wrong: He asks whether someone has already used this computer
He offers to let her use this computer
He asks her to lend him her own computer

lines: 田中さんって、怒りっぽいところさえなければ、いい人なんだけどね。
96.en: Tanaka would be a good person except for his short temper
wrong: Tanaka is a good person because he never gets angry
Tanaka is leaving the company, which is a shame
Tanaka is a good person, and his temper is his best point

lines: 会議、予定より早く終わりそうもないね。
97.en: The meeting does not look like it will end earlier than planned
wrong: The meeting looks like it will end earlier than planned
The meeting has already ended ahead of schedule
The meeting is expected to start later than planned

lines: あの店のケーキ、並んででも食べる価値あるよ。
98.en: That shop's cake is worth eating even if you must queue
wrong: That shop's cake is not worth queuing for
That shop's cake can be bought without queuing
That shop's cake is too expensive to buy often

lines: もう少しで乗り遅れるところだったよ。
99.en: He nearly missed the train but made it in time
wrong: He missed the train and had to wait for the next one
He got on early and had plenty of time to spare
He wants to apologize for making others miss the train

lines: 明日の打ち合わせ、私が出るまでもないですよね。
100.en: She thinks there is no need for her to attend tomorrow's meeting
wrong: She wants very much to attend tomorrow's meeting
She asks whether tomorrow's meeting has already started
She plans to leave tomorrow's meeting early

lines: 四つ目にしようかな。
だから、僕が習って教えるよ。
101.en: He leans to the fourth course, then decides to learn it and teach his father

lines: 書道は道具をそろえるのが大変そうで。今回は写真にする。
102.en: Calligraphy needs too many tools, so this time she will take photography
wrong: She will take calligraphy even though the tools are costly
She will take the book repair course for an old album
She will take the computer course to learn email

lines: あの、会社の屋上はどうですか。
じゃあ、それでいこう。食事は業者に頼んで、運んでもらおう。
103.en: The company roof is proposed and the boss agrees to use it, with catering
wrong: The boss decides on the meeting room because of possible rain
The boss picks the restaurant's private room instead
The boss agrees to the pub near the station

lines: 個室は二十人までのところが多いんですよ。今年は参加者が二十八人なので。
104.en: Private rooms usually seat up to twenty, but twenty-eight are coming
wrong: Private rooms are usually too expensive for twenty-eight people
Private rooms usually seat thirty, so twenty-eight fit
Only twenty people are coming, so a private room is enough
